result:
Created `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/InstantsAgentTest.java` covering all four documented methods of `Instants`:

- **`toEpochMillis`**: ordinary instant, `Instant.EPOCH`, negative millis, `null` (treated as epoch → 0), and overflow bounds (`Instant.MAX` → `Long.MAX_VALUE`, `Instant.MIN` → `Long.MIN_VALUE`).
- **`toInstant(Instant)`**: non-null pass-through, `null` → `Instant.EPOCH`.
- **`toInstant(Instant, Instant)`**: non-null pass-through (default ignored, even if default is null), `null` → default, both `null` → `null`.
- **`toMillisSince`**: near-zero for `Instant.now()`, epoch/`null` approximating `System.currentTimeMillis()`, and overflow bounds (`Instant.MAX` → `Long.MIN_VALUE`, `Instant.MIN` → `Long.MAX_VALUE`).

I verified the overflow-direction assumptions against actual JDK `Instant`/`Duration` behavior in a throwaway scratch script (not part of the library under test) before writing the assertions, then removed the scratch file. `./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
